simple.meaning: עָתָר (ʻâthâr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “incense (as increasing to a volume of smoke); hence a worshipper.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Ezekiel, Zephaniah, beginning at Ezekiel 8:11. Its contexts include family line, offering, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָתָר (H6282).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: incense (as increasing to a volume of smoke); hence a worshipper
definitions.full: H6282. athar I. [ עָתַר ] noun [masculine] suppliant, worshipper (?; so usually, but dubious); — only plural suffix עֲתָרַי Zeph 3:10 . II. [ עָתָר ] noun [masculine] odour (si vera lectio) (so Vrss.); — construct עֲתַר Ezek 8:11 , of incense.

occurrences.englishText: Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel stood before them. In the middle of them Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan stood, every man with his censer in his hand; and the smell of the cloud of incense went up.
From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers, even the daughter of my dispersed people, will bring my offering.
